subject: PrivDeploy module compatibility matrix and CI deprecation plan
messages:
From: Lisa Rivera <lisa.rivera@acme.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: ops-team@acme.com; marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-18T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PrivDeploy module compatibility check-in

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the demo last week. Our platform team ran the staging deploy and hit a couple of regressions tied to module pinning and an older Helm chart format. We discussed a compatibility matrix in the call — can Redwood produce an initial matrix that maps: Terraform module versions, Helm chart API versions, Ansible role names, and the corresponding CI jobs that validate them?

Main asks:
- Which module versions are considered stable (we want a pinned set for our procurement SLA).
- Planned deprecations for any modules that will be removed in the next two quarters.
- A list of CI jobs that Acme should keep green to avoid breaking upgrades.

If you can send a short matrix + a proposed deprecation schedule we can route it through procurement and our SRE review. Attaching the staging logs we referenced.

Thanks,
Lisa
Acme Platform

Attachment stubs: staging-deploy-20260517.log (text)

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
To: Lisa Rivera <lisa.rivera@acme.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com; karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-18T10:38:00-07:00
Subject: RE: PrivDeploy module compatibility check-in

Lisa — thanks for the clear asks. I pulled together an initial compatibility matrix (attached: privdeploy-compat-matrix-v1.xlsx) and a draft CI job index (ci-job-list.md). Highlights up-front:

- Stable set: terraform/modules/v1.12.x, helm/charts/v2 (kube 1.24+), ansible/roles/v3.1.x are what we consider GA for Private deployments today.
- Planned deprecations: tf module "networking-legacy" will be deprecated on 2026-09-01 (replaced by "networking-v2"). We recommend a two-phase window: opt-in compatibility warning for 8 weeks, then hard deprecation.
- CI jobs: pipeline names and quick descriptions included in ci-job-list.md. Key ones for you: "privdeploy/tf-compat-check" (matrix test across TF versions), "privdeploy/helm-api-lint" (detects old Chart API fields), and "privdeploy/ansible-role-smoke" (runbook idempotence check).

Action items we propose:
1) Redwood to run the matrix against Acme staging (we can provision a 3-day test window) — I can own scheduling.
2) Karthik to propose the deprecation announcement text and version migration steps.
3) Marissa to confirm evidence artifacts that procurement needs (SLOs, test run logs).

Do you want us to convert the matrix into a CSV for your procurement trackers?

— Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Partner Solutions, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: privdeploy-compat-matrix-v1.xlsx, ci-job-list.md

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com; marissa_cole@redwood.com; vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: Lisa Rivera <lisa.rivera@acme.com>
Date: 2026-05-19T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PrivDeploy module compatibility check-in

Looping in some technical detail for the deprecation plan and CI integration. Notes below and proposed schedule.

On Tue, May 18, 2026 at 10:38 AM Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com> wrote:
> - Planned deprecations: tf module "networking-legacy" will be deprecated on 2026-09-01...

Technical notes:
- Migration approach: create a compatibility shim in networking-v2 that accepts legacy variable names for two releases; add a tfupgrade CI job that runs 'terraform 0.13-to-latest' compatibility checks.
- Helm: we'll add a chart-transform test that fails the current helm-api-lint job if Chart.yaml apiVersion == "v1" and uses deprecated hooks. This prevents silent upgrades when Acme's repo is still on older chart formats.
- Ansible: add role-version metadata to meta/main.yml and bump role idempotence checks in ansible-role-smoke.

CI orchestration: recommendation is to publish a small GitLab CI template (we already have a draft: templates/privdeploy-compat.yml) that Acme can include. It contains the matrix axes: TF versions [1.2.x, 1.3.x], Kube versions [1.24, 1.25], Helm [v2,v3]. If Acme is moving to ArgoCD later, the template is portable as it outputs artifacts and test result junit XML which Argo/argo-rollouts can consume.

Proposed timeline:
- 2026-06-01: Redwood runs staged compatibility sweep (we'll create MR with test results).
- 2026-07-15: Public compatibility report + procurement evidence package.
- 2026-09-01: Start hard deprecation on networking-legacy (abort if >5 major breakages).

I'll attach a minimal patch for the tf module that adds the shim (tf-module-change-log.patch). Feedback welcome.

- Karthik
Sr. Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: tf-module-change-log.patch

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com; karthik_iyer@redwood.com; vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: Lisa Rivera <lisa.rivera@acme.com>
Date: 2026-05-20T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: RE: PrivDeploy module compatibility check-in

Thanks Karthik — this looks actionable. Quick procurement/ops notes:

- Procurement wants a single CSV with: module, current_version, stable_pin, deprecation_date, migration_guide_link. Stephanie — can you convert the matrix to that format?
- Acme SRE wants the CI job names to include a stable slug so they can whitelist in their pipeline config: suggestion pattern "privdeploy-compat-<tool>-<major>". I'll standardize the names in ci-job-list.md and push a small MR to the templates repo.
- We should also add a rollback playbook entry to the private deployment runbook (runbooks/privdeploy-rollback.md) describing how Acme can pin older modules in the event they need to pause. Vivek — can you own the playbook snippet?

I'll start drafting the procurement evidence package once the CSV arrives. Stephanie — please go ahead and convert the matrix and schedule the 3-day sweep for week of 2026-06-01. I'll coordinate the MR for the CI template naming.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Product Operations, Redwood Inference
snippet: Initial Acme ask for compatibility matrix + deprecation schedule; Redwood team proposes matrix, CI template, and migration timeline. Action items: schedule sweep, convert matrix to CSV, produce procurement evidence, publish CI template, add rollback playbook snippet.
